output.metric: Daily totals exceed the weekly rollup
output.observed_change: Summing the daily signup table over a week gives a number about 9 percent higher than the weekly rollup for the same period.
output.notes: A genuine marketing campaign started mid-window.

blind_spots: marts.signups has no recorded owners — no accountable team on record for this dataset.
staging.events_weekly_rollup (the comparison target named in the symptom) also has no recorded owners.

raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw both have null field-level schema and empty custom_properties, so nothing is recorded about dedup keys, event-type filters, or how is_automated is applied upstream of either path.

Asymmetric sourcing: staging.events_daily (feeds the daily signup table) draws from both raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw, while staging.events_weekly_rollup draws only from raw.channel_events_raw — the daily path has a source the weekly path lacks, and this hasn't been confirmed as intentional.

Timezone mismatch on record: events_daily buckets on local time, events_weekly_rollup buckets on UTC. The exact boundary-conversion logic between them is not captured in any schema or description read so far.

raw.web_sessions' is_automated flag is documented as inconsistently set by producers — whether bot/automated traffic is being filtered differently (or at all) on the daily vs. weekly path is unconfirmed.
No assertion or data-quality-test lookup was available, so nothing is known about whether either dataset has failing checks around the campaign start date.

output.statement: The daily signups table (via staging.events_daily) overcounts because it unions raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw without deduplicating conversions that fire into both raw sources, while the weekly rollup sources only from raw.channel_events_raw and so never sees the overlap; the campaign amplified the gap by driving more dual-tracked traffic through both raw paths.
would_be_confirmed_by: A sample of signup/session identifiers from raw.web_sessions during the campaign window matches identifiers already present in raw.channel_events_raw for the same conversion event.
Excluding rows attributable to raw.web_sessions from the daily table's weekly sum brings the total within a small margin (e.g. <1%) of the weekly rollup figure.
The size of the overlap between the two raw sources grows proportionally with campaign-driven traffic volume.
would_be_refuted_by: The events_daily transformation contains an explicit join/dedup key (e.g. on session_id or conversion_id) that already excludes double-sourced events before aggregation.
A sample of signup identifiers in events_daily during the window shows no rows sourced from both raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw for the same underlying conversion.

Removing all web_sessions-attributable rows from the daily sum still leaves the total materially above (or the gap unchanged from) the weekly rollup, showing the discrepancy isn't explained by source overlap.

output.statement: The 9% gap is a definitional artifact, not a data defect: staging.events_daily buckets signup timestamps in local time while staging.events_weekly_rollup buckets in UTC, so summing daily local-time buckets does not correspond to the exact UTC week window used by the rollup; the resulting boundary-shifted slice of signups inflates the daily sum, and this shows up more visibly in the campaign window because the campaign concentrated signup volume in time-of-day bursts that fall disproportionately into the mismatched boundary hours.
would_be_confirmed_by: The local timezone configured for events_daily has a non-zero UTC offset documented in the dbt model config, column metadata, or session config.
The daily-vs-weekly gap size correlates with the volume of signups occurring near local midnight (the hours that fall in the mismatched offset window).
Re-bucketing events_daily signups to UTC before summing and re-comparing to the weekly rollup closes most of the 9% gap.
would_be_refuted_by: Re-aligning daily buckets to UTC day boundaries and re-summing still leaves roughly the same ~9% gap versus the weekly rollup.
The local timezone used by events_daily has zero UTC offset, making a boundary shift impossible.
The gap is uniform in magnitude across weeks far from the campaign and shows no concentration near day/week boundaries, indicating a non-boundary cause dominates.

output.statement: The is_automated flag on raw.web_sessions is set inconsistently by upstream producers, and staging.events_daily fails to filter on it while the weekly rollup's exclusive channel_events_raw path effectively excludes automated traffic; the campaign drove a surge of bot/automated web session hits that staging.events_daily counted as signups but the weekly rollup never saw, producing the 9% gap.
would_be_confirmed_by: Row-level audit of staging.events_daily shows signups sourced from web_sessions with is_automated=true, with no filter applied in the transformation logic.
The volume of is_automated=true web_sessions rows during the campaign window, when summed, accounts for approximately the 9 percent discrepancy.
channel_events_raw records show no equivalent automated-traffic contamination, or its transformation applies filtering that web_sessions' does not.
would_be_refuted_by: staging.events_daily's transformation SQL already excludes is_automated=true rows from web_sessions at the same rate as the weekly path.
Excluding all is_automated=true records from the daily sum still leaves a gap close to 9 percent, unchanged from before exclusion.
The is_automated flag shows no unusual increase in true values during the campaign window relative to the size of the observed gap.

output.narrative: staging.events_daily draws from two upstream sources (raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw) while staging.events_weekly_rollup draws from only one (raw.channel_events_raw). This asymmetry is confirmed independently from three separate lineage query directions — UPSTREAM from events_daily (e1, e13), UPSTREAM from events_weekly_rollup (e2, e14), and DOWNSTREAM from channel_events_raw (e3) — all mutually consistent and never directly refuted. Because the 'same period' daily and weekly aggregates are not actually built from the same underlying source set, they are not apples-to-apples: the extra web_sessions source in the daily path is the best-evidenced explanation for the ~9% gap, independent of the coincident marketing campaign (which would inflate both aggregates equally if sourcing were symmetric). No dedup or join key excluding source overlap is documented in the catalog for events_daily (e4), and neither raw.web_sessions nor staging.events_daily carry any assertions that would catch this overlap (e5, e6). Row-level confirmation of the exact overlap mechanism (duplicate conversion IDs across the two raw sources) could not be obtained because warehouse.query is not connected in this run (e17), so confidence is moderate rather than high.

steps.rationale: Root-cause confidence is only 0.55 because the row-level reconciliation query needed to confirm the web_sessions/channel_events_raw overlap could not be run (warehouse.query unavailable in this run). events_daily unions raw.web_sessions and raw.channel_events_raw with no documented dedup or join key (custom_properties empty, fields null), while events_weekly_rollup sources only from raw.channel_events_raw. This asymmetry was independently confirmed from three lineage directions (UPSTREAM of events_daily, UPSTREAM of events_weekly_rollup, DOWNSTREAM of channel_events_raw) and never refuted. Only apply this step once step 1 confirms the overlap; the fix should either dedup on a shared conversion/session identifier or, if web_sessions represents genuinely distinct signups, that must be a documented product decision rather than an accidental gap.

Neither dataset currently carries any DataHub-recorded assertions, so a sourcing drift like this one has no automated detection today. Add a scheduled check comparing the weekly sum of events_daily against events_weekly_rollup for the same period, alerting if divergence exceeds a small threshold (e.g. 2%).

Both datasets have no recorded owners in the catalog, so there is no accountable team to approve the sourcing decision in step 2 or to review the new assertion in step 3. This is an operational fix independent of the specific root cause.
